title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week in the space and defense sector saw a mix of testing, funding, and strategic partnerships. As established players like SpaceX continue to push boundaries, financial pressures and geopolitical interests are reshaping the landscape for emerging companies and defense initiatives.

themes.title: SpaceX's Starship Progress
themes.body: SpaceX completed its 13th Starship test flight, inching closer to operational readiness. This relentless pace underscores the company's commitment to dominating the launch market, despite the occasional hiccup.

themes.title: Financial Struggles for ULA
themes.body: United Launch Alliance is grappling with financial challenges stemming from the grounding of its Vulcan rocket. This situation highlights the precarious nature of relying on new technology in a competitive environment.

themes.title: Defense Tech IPOs on the Horizon
themes.body: The defense-tech IPO window appears to be cracking open, with several companies eyeing public offerings. This could signal a shift in investor appetite, as the sector seeks to capitalize on heightened interest in national security.

themes.title: AI's Growing Role in Defense
themes.body: LatConnect 60's unveiling of AI capabilities reflects a broader trend of integrating advanced technology into defense strategies. As every startup seems to pivot towards 'AI for Defense,' the challenge will be differentiating genuine innovation from mere buzz.
